newsitem.title: CHINA: China issues revised collateral rules.
newsitem.headline: China issues revised collateral rules.

text.p: China on Thursday issued new rules widening the range of items that can be used by both local and foreign-related firms as collateral to guarantee loans.

The new rules, published in the Finance Times, allow companies to use bank guarantees, fixed assets and real estate mortgages as collateral. The previous rules did not cover foreign-invested firms and only allowed the use of bank guarantees.
The new rules, issued by the People's Bank of China, said both local currency and foreign exchange could now be used for collateral.
The Finance Times quoted a spokesman for the central bank as saying that new rules were promulgated because the old ones were now out-of-date given the pace of financial reform.
The amount used as collateral by a non-financial body must not exceed 50 percent of its net assets and the firm's annual foreign exchange income, the rules said.
The former rules said the amount must not exceed the foreign exchange held by a firm.
